materials.title: STATS 315 Syllabus
pages: STATS 315: Statistics I, Fall 2026. Probability, random variables, common distributions, sampling distributions, the central limit theorem, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
Grading: homework 20%, quizzes 10%, data analysis project 15%, Midterm 1 15%, Midterm 2 15%, final exam 25%.
Homework is due Mondays at 11:59 PM on Canvas. Late homework is not accepted, but the lowest homework score is dropped.

materials.title: Chapter 6 slides: Normal Distribution and CLT
pages: The normal distribution is symmetric and bell-shaped, described by its mean mu and standard deviation sigma.
Standardize with z = (x - mu) / sigma to use the standard normal table.
The central limit theorem: for a large sample size n, the sample mean is approximately normal with mean mu and standard deviation sigma / sqrt(n), whatever the shape of the population.
Rule of thumb: n >= 30 is usually enough for the CLT approximation unless the population is very skewed.

materials.title: Chapter 7 slides: Confidence Intervals
pages: A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for a population parameter: estimate plus or minus margin of error.
For a mean with known sigma: x-bar plus or minus z* times sigma / sqrt(n). For 95% confidence, z* = 1.96.
A 95% confidence level means that 95% of intervals built this way would contain the true mean; it is not the probability that this particular interval contains it.
Larger samples give narrower intervals; higher confidence gives wider intervals.
